title: talaria.json — a Talaria app's manifest
description: The manifest at the root of every app. Install and update refuse a manifest that fails these rules, with the reason; an installed app whose manifest fails is listed in Manage → Apps as broken and can still be uninstalled. The rules run in the host (talaria-app-manifest in Rust, ui/src/server/app-build/manifest.ts in TS), pinned to one shared fixture; this schema is their published shape. Keys not listed here are ignored.

$schema.description: This schema's URL, for editors. Ignored by the host.

name.description: The app's display name. Required, and not only whitespace.

slug.description: The slug the app installs as: its path segment under /x and /api/apps. Install uses it instead of deriving one from the repository's name, refuses an admin's different slug, and refuses one already taken. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes; not a word the client router reserves. An installed app whose directory differs from its declared slug is listed as broken.

icon.description: A glyph or emoji for the dock tile. Default ⬡.

version.description: The app's own version, shown in Manage → Apps. Default 0.0.0. Updates follow git commits, not this field.

surfaces.description: The UI surfaces the app declares, each with its title. Declaring any requires app.ts; an app with none is server- or MCP-only.

sdk.description: The @talaria/sdk range the app was written against, in npm's range grammar without pre-release tags or hyphen ranges ("^1.0", ">=1.2 <2", "1.x", "^1 || ^2"). A host whose SDK version (x-talaria-sdk-version above, for this revision) is outside the range refuses to install the app and lists an installed one as broken.

harnesses.description: Reserved for the app harness registry. Its shape is checked; nothing reads it yet.

triggers.description: Reserved for scheduled and event triggers. Each names an id and exactly one of cron or event, as a string that is not only whitespace; nothing runs them yet.
